questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.topic: Isolating the principal in a formula
questions.learningObjective: isolate a variable in a product formula
questions.stem: Solve A equals P(1 plus r t) for P. If A equals 110, r equals 0.1, and t equals 1, what is P? Report the number only.
questions.explanation: Dividing both sides by (1 plus r t) gives P equals A divided by (1 plus r t), so P equals 110 divided by 1.1, which is 100. Substituting back gives 100 times 1.1 equals 110. Dividing by only r or only t gives a wrong principal.
questions.hint: Divide the amount by (1 plus r t).

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.stem: Which transformation can change the solution set of an equation?

options.text: Multiplying both sides by 4, because scaling changes the value of x
options.misconception: thinks multiplying by a nonzero number changes solutions

options.text: Adding 3 to both sides, because constants change the balance
options.misconception: believes adding the same constant changes solutions

options.text: Taking the square root of both sides, because it can drop a negative solution
Subtracting x from both sides, because the variable disappears
options.misconception: believes moving a variable term removes solutions

questions.explanation: Adding, subtracting, multiplying, or dividing both sides by the same nonzero quantity preserves solutions. Taking the square root of both sides is not reversible and can discard a negative solution. The trap is confusing reversible operations with non-reversible ones.
questions.hint: Ask whether the operation can be undone uniquely.

questions.stem: Solve 6x plus 3 equals 2x plus 19. What is x? Report the number only.
questions.explanation: Subtracting 2x gives 4x plus 3 equals 19, then subtracting 3 gives 4x equals 16, so x equals 4. Checking gives 27 on both sides. Moving the variable to the side with the larger coefficient keeps the arithmetic simple.
questions.hint: Subtract the smaller variable term first.

options.misconception: adds the conversion factor

options.text: v equals 1.2 times 1000, because millilitres are smaller than litres

questions.explanation: Since millilitres are smaller, the count increases: 1.2 litres times 1000 millilitres per litre gives 1200 millilitres. Dividing would give a fraction of a litre.

options.misconception: uses the percent as a whole number multiplier

options.text: c equals 0.72 times 50, because the percent of the total is the part correct
c equals 50 divided by 0.72, because the count is found by sharing
options.misconception: divides by the percent

options.text: c equals 50 minus 72, because the percent is subtracted
options.misconception: subtracts the percent from the total

questions.explanation: Seventy-two percent means 0.72, so the number correct is 0.72 times 50, which is 36. Using 72 as a multiplier gives a count above the total.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.stem: A pharmacist mixes 8 litres of 15 percent solution with x litres of 25 percent solution to get a 20 percent mixture. Which equation balances the solute?

options.text: 8 plus x equals 0.20 times 0.15, because total volume equals a percent of concentration
options.misconception: confuses total volume with solute amount

options.text: 0.15 plus 0.25 equals 0.20 times x, because concentrations add directly
options.misconception: adds concentrations without weighting by volume

options.text: 0.15 times 8 plus 0.25 times x equals 0.20 times (8 plus x), because solute before equals solute after
0.15 times 8 equals 0.25 times x, because the two solute amounts must match
options.misconception: forces the two contributions to be equal

questions.explanation: Solute from each part is concentration times volume, and the final solute is 0.20 times the total volume. Equating those balances the mixture. Adding concentrations or forcing equality ignores the volumes.
questions.hint: Multiply each concentration by its volume before adding.

options.misconception: inverts speed and distance

options.text: 60 times t equals 210, because speed times time equals distance

questions.stem: Ben is 7 years older than Chloe. In 5 years Ben will be twice as old as Chloe is now. Which equation finds Chloe's current age c?

options.text: c plus 7 plus 5 equals 2 times c, because Ben's future age equals twice Chloe's current age
c plus 5 equals 2 times (c plus 7), because the age gap is doubled
options.misconception: doubles Ben's current age instead

options.text: c plus 12 equals 2 times c, because the gap grows by 5
options.misconception: adds the time to the age gap

questions.explanation: Ben's current age is c plus 7, and in 5 years it is c plus 12, which equals 2 times c. The trap is doubling the wrong age or misplacing the 5 years.

options.text: Original gives y equals 5, rearranged gives 2 equals (5 plus 3) divided by 4, which is 2, so it checks

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.stem: Two lines on a graph are the same line. What does that tell you about the system?

options.text: The system has no solution, because the lines overlap
options.misconception: confuses overlapping with parallel distinct

options.text: The system has infinitely many solutions, because every point on the line works
The system has exactly one solution, because two lines give one crossing
options.misconception: assumes two lines always give one solution

options.text: The system has two solutions, one for each line
options.misconception: counts individual line solutions

questions.explanation: When two equations describe the same line, every point on that line satisfies both, so the solution set is infinite. No solution would require parallel distinct lines.
questions.hint: Overlapping lines share all their points.

questions.stem: The system is 3x plus 2y equals 4 and 6x plus 4y equals 10. How many solutions does it have?

options.text: Exactly one, because there are two equations
options.misconception: assumes two equations always give one solution

options.text: Infinitely many, because the coefficients are proportional
options.misconception: ignores that the constant must also be proportional

options.text: None, because the second left side is twice the first but the constant is not
Exactly two, one for each equation
options.misconception: counts individual equation solutions

questions.explanation: The left side of the second equation is exactly twice the first, but the right side 10 is not twice 4. That gives parallel distinct lines with no common point. Proportional coefficients alone are not enough; the constant must scale by the same factor.
